Recent advances in artificial intelligence have transformed multiple scientific disciplines (Brown, 2019). In natural language processing, large language models have achieved unprecedented performance on benchmark tasks (Chen, 2020), while simultaneously raising concerns about computational costs (Davis, 2021). Computer vision has likewise benefited from deep convolutional architectures (Lee, 2018) and attention-based mechanisms adapted from NLP research (Wang, 2020). In computational biology, protein structure prediction has been revolutionized by transformer models (Patel, 2021), enabling new drug discovery pipelines (Kim, 2022). The intersection of these advances presents both opportunities and challenges for interdisciplinary collaboration (Smith et al., 2023).
